# INV-USD-001 again, with a `payment:` block naming the bank transaction and
# the split that was parked in the CAD account.
#
# Q-039. The settlement is USD throughout — USD invoice, USD receivable, USD
# bank — and 100 USD arrived against 100 USD owed, so `amount: 100` is the
# payment and no rate is stated because nothing converts. The split named in
# `txn_split_guid:` is the CAD one, which is the point: it stood in for the
# receivable while nobody knew what the money was, and linking the payment is
# what replaces it.
#
# The invoice block repeats what the book already holds, because a posted
# invoice takes a `payment:` block and nothing else. Every other line is
# fx_usd_invoice_cad_income.txt's, unchanged.
#
# What this fixture produces: the transaction becomes
#   Assets:Bank:USD                 +100.00 USD
#   Assets:Accounts Receivable USD  -100.00 USD   in the invoice's lot
# quoted in USD, with no CAD left in it.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-25
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    txn_guid: "c9f27c2b2f324117aa17c7c1f48fbafd"
    txn_split_guid: "614b338df4f94c359aa35ffacc2dadcf"
